digest.component_or_area: ADR (Architecture Decision Record) management and numbering system
propositions: 91 ADR files contain 17 duplicate numbers (22 files assigned to collision groups), creating ambiguity when ADRs are referenced by number alone

The root cause is stale-base merges (16 of 22 collisions) and Gerrit races (6 of 22), both preventable by a per-number marker file mechanism (`docs/adr/.numbers/NNNN`) that creates add/add conflicts on duplicate claims

Cross-references to collision-group numbers in docs/ and src/ must be disambiguated and rewritten to point to the final (renumbered) ADR, with resolution tiers (slug-exact, topic-matched, ancestry, UNRESOLVED) recorded in RENUMBERING.md

A CI check (`scripts/check_adr_numbers.py`) must enforce bijection between ADR files and marker files, assert all numbers are distinct, verify marker content uniqueness, and validate all `adr/NNNN-slug` links resolve to existing files
Renumbering assigns 22 duplicate-numbered ADRs to the range 0070-0091 in ascending landing-date order, with earliest-landed ADRs in each collision group retaining their original numbers
A generated `docs/adr/README.md` index grouped by workstream and a `RENUMBERING.md` mapping (old→new and per-reference resolution table) provide the definitive reference for the renumbered corpus
